note: Native first. Every recipe leads with a platform API, because the browser already ships the animation primitives most interfaces need. A library appears only where the platform genuinely cannot do the job, and then it comes with the exact install line so the agent can stop, install, and continue.

recipes.name: Skeleton screen
recipes.oneLiner: Hold the layout while content loads, so nothing jumps.
notes: Announce the wait: `aria-busy="true"` on the region, and `aria-live="polite"` so the swap is spoken.
Skeletons must match the real layout's line count and widths, or the load causes exactly the jump they were meant to prevent.
Under reduced motion the sweep stops; the block stays.
recipes.fallback: If the wait is under ~300ms, show nothing: a skeleton that flashes is worse than a blank frame.

recipes.name: Indeterminate loading bar
recipes.oneLiner: A thin bar that says work is happening, without a spinner.
notes: Animate `inset-inline-start` or `transform`, never `width`: width triggers layout on every frame.
A determinate bar needs `aria-valuenow`; this one is indeterminate, so it has no value attributes.
Three pixels is the visible minimum; below that it reads as a border artefact.
recipes.fallback: For anything over ~2s, prefer a determinate bar driven by real progress; an indeterminate bar beats a spinner only for short waits.

recipes.name: Reveal on scroll
recipes.oneLiner: Sections settle in as they enter the viewport.
recipes.snippet:
<style>
@supports (animation-timeline: view()) {
  .reveal {
    animation: reveal-in linear both;
    animation-timeline: view();
    animation-range: entry 10% cover 30%;
  }
  @keyframes reveal-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(24px) } to { opacity: 1; transform: none } }
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .reveal { animation: none } }
</style>
<section class="reveal">…</section>
notes: Scroll-driven animations run on the compositor and need no scroll listener, so they cost nothing per frame.
Wrap in `@supports (animation-timeline: view())`; the unsupported branch shows the content normally, not invisible.
Keep the travel under ~32px. Anything larger fights the scroll instead of riding it.
recipes.fallback: Where scroll-driven animations are unavailable, add a single `IntersectionObserver` that toggles a class; do not compute positions in a scroll handler.

recipes.name: Shared element transition
recipes.oneLiner: A card grows into the page it opens, so the user keeps their place.
recipes.snippet:
<style>
.card-thumb { view-transition-name: product-media; }
::view-transition-old(product-media), ::view-transition-new(product-media) { animation-duration: 240ms; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { ::view-transition-group(*), ::view-transition-old(*), ::view-transition-new(*) { animation: none !important } }
</style>
<script>
function navigate(update) {
  if (!document.startViewTransition) { update(); return }
  document.startViewTransition(update)
}
</script>
notes: The name must be unique per snapshot: give it to exactly one element, or the transition is dropped silently.
Old and new roots are snapshots, so animating inside them costs nothing.
Browser support is now broad enough to use as the default path; keep the `if` guard for the rest.
recipes.fallback: No view transitions: keep the normal navigation and let the new page scroll-restore. Do not fake it with a FLIP clone unless the transition is the point of the page.

recipes.name: Context menu
recipes.oneLiner: A menu at the pointer or on a row's right-click, dismissed by Escape and outside clicks.
notes: `popover` gives Escape, light dismiss, and top-layer stacking for free — the three things hand-rolled menus get wrong.
For pointer positioning use `position-area` / anchor positioning where available, and fall back to the coordinates above.
`role="menu"` plus `role="menuitem"` obliges arrow-key movement; if you skip the keys, use links and buttons without the menu roles.
recipes.fallback: Inside a table with many rows, one menu element reused per row keeps the DOM small; move the popover rather than creating one per row.

recipes.name: Toast notification
recipes.oneLiner: A short confirmation that does not steal focus.
notes: `aria-live="polite"` announces without interrupting; use `assertive` only for errors the user must act on.
Do not move focus to a toast. If the message needs a decision, it is a dialog, not a toast.
Auto-dismiss after 4–6s, and never dismiss something the user is reading — pause the timer on hover and focus.
recipes.fallback: Persistent toasts for anything the user must acknowledge; transient ones for confirmations only.

recipes.name: Hover lift
recipes.oneLiner: A small raise on pointer devices that signals the surface is interactive.
recipes.snippet:
<style>
.lift { transition: transform 160ms cubic-bezier(.2, .8, .2, 1), box-shadow 160ms ease; }
@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) {
  .lift:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: var(--uiux-shadow-lg, 0 10px 24px rgb(0 0 0 / .12)); }
}
.lift:active { transform: translateY(0); }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .lift, .lift:hover { transition: none; transform: none } }
</style>
notes: Guard with `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`: without it, touch devices keep the lifted state after a tap.
Two pixels is a lift; eight is a bounce. The scale of the style decides, and the style's `motion` tokens give the duration.
Lift must never be the only affordance — a card that only looks clickable on hover is invisible to keyboards.
recipes.fallback: Reduce or remove under `prefers-reduced-motion`; the card stays clickable.

recipes.name: Spring entrance for a list
recipes.oneLiner: Staggered spring entrance where the platform's easing cannot express overshoot.
recipes.snippet:
<script type="module">
import { animate, stagger } from 'motion'

animate('.row', { opacity: [0, 1], y: [12, 0] }, { delay: stagger(0.04), type: 'spring', stiffness: 320, damping: 30 })
</script>
notes: Reach for this only when CSS `linear()` easing cannot express the motion; `linear()` covers most spring curves with zero bytes.
Run it after paint, and skip it entirely under `prefers-reduced-motion` by checking `matchMedia` first.
Stagger above ~60ms per item starts to feel slow beyond eight items; cap the total.
recipes.fallback: CSS only: `transition` with a `linear()` easing plus `transition-delay: calc(var(--i) * 40ms)` per row.

deps.name: motion
deps.why: The maintained successor to Framer Motion's imperative API; ~4 kB gzipped for `animate` + `stagger`.
